To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular mechanisms underlying cell proliferation of olfactory epithelum progenitor cells are complex and involve cyclin D1 and cdk2 and cd4, which are differentially regulated during mitotic stimulation.
the molecular mechanisms underlying cell‐cycle control in neuronal progenitor cells have been investigated using adult mouse olfactory‐neuron progenitors as a model.

the mitotic stimulation of olfactory neuron progenitors after lesioning of their synaptic target, the olfactory bulb, involves a rise of cyclin D/cdk complexes, with differential activation of cdk2 versus cdk4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying cell division in neuronal cells.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the proliferation of adult olfactory epitheliamitotic cells in response to olfactory bulb ablation.
the molecular mechanisms underlying cell division in olfactory neuronal lineage progenitor cells in adult mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mitotic stimulation of neuronal progenitors in olfactory epithelum is characterized by the activation of cyclin‐dependent kinases (cdk2 and cdk 4), in particular, by their binding to the cyclin D, and the down‐regulation of their inhibitors (p27 and p21).
the olfactory system in the adult mouse is a useful model for the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying cell proliferation in the nervous system.
cyclin D1 and cyclins E and D1/cdks 2 and 4 are involved in olfactory neuron mitotic stimulation, with differential regulation of cdk2/cdk4 complexes and of cdk2 kinase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cyclin D1, a key regulator of cell cycle, is regulated in a very unusual fashion in the in vivo mitotic response of neuronal progenitors in olfactory epithelum of adult mouse, with differential activation of cyclin D/cdk2 and of cyclin D/ cdk4.
the olfactory system has a unique ability to undergo a mitotic reaction in the adult.
olfactory neuron progenitor cell cycle is controlled in vivo by the balance between cdk4 and cdk2 activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the olfactory neuron progenitors are a very good model system for the study of cell cycle regulation in vivo.
the cyclin/cdk complexes that control G1 phase entry in the cell cycle are regulated in a very unusual manner in olfactory neuron progenitors.
the olfactory epithelum of the mouse is a good model to study the cell cycle.
